_meta.source: Standard aqueous solubility rules for high school general chemistry (Opus 15 / Atkins style solubility table).
_meta.ionPlainConvention: ionPlain is the ASCII form the solubility UI parses, e.g. "SO4^2-", "OH-", "NH4+". ionFormula is the display form with unicode superscripts.

rules.rule: All group 1 metal cations form soluble compounds
rules.note: Li2CO3 is the least soluble of the group 1 carbonates

rules.rule: All group 1 metal cations form soluble compounds
rules.note: The only common exception is insoluble sodium magnesium carbonate in cold concentrated solution

rules.rule: All group 1 metal cations form soluble compounds
All group 1 metal cations form soluble compounds
All group 1 metal cations form soluble compounds
All ammonium salts are soluble in water
Beryllium compounds are soluble but Be2+ hydrolyses water and turns solutions acidic
rules.note: Be(OH)2 is insoluble, so strongly basic solutions give a white precipitate

rules.rule: Most magnesium salts are soluble
rules.note: Magnesium hydroxide is only slightly soluble

rules.rule: Most calcium salts are soluble, including the chloride, nitrate and sulfate
rules.note: Calcium carbonate, phosphate, sulfite, hydroxide and oxalate are insoluble

rules.rule: Most strontium salts are soluble
rules.note: Strontium carbonate, phosphate, sulfate and hydroxide are insoluble or slightly soluble

rules.rule: Most barium salts are soluble
rules.note: Barium sulfate and barium carbonate are insoluble, which is why barium meals show up on X-rays

rules.rule: All nitrates are soluble in water
rules.note: Nitrates are the most soluble group of salts

rules.rule: All nitrites are soluble in water
All acetates are soluble in water
rules.note: Silver and mercury acetates are only slightly soluble

rules.rule: All chlorates are soluble in water
rules.note: Potassium chlorate is only sparingly soluble in cold water

rules.rule: All perchlorates are soluble in water
All cyanides are soluble in water
rules.note: Heavy metal cyanides such as AgCN and CuCN are insoluble

rules.rule: Most thiocyanates are soluble
rules.note: Silver thiocyanate is insoluble

rules.rule: Most sulfates are soluble in water
rules.exceptions: exceptions: Ba²⁺, Sr²⁺, Pb²⁺, Ca²⁺, Ag⁺
rules.note: Barium sulfate is so insoluble it stays white in the stomach and shows on an X-ray

rules.rule: Sulfites of the group 1 metals and ammonium are soluble; most other sulfites are not
rules.note: Sulfites decompose in acid, releasing sulphur dioxide gas

rules.rule: Hydrogen sulfate is soluble and is the acidic form of sulfate
rules.note: Converts to sulfate when the solution is made alkaline

rules.rule: Most chlorides are soluble in water
rules.note: Silver chloride precipitates white and dissolves in ammonia

rules.rule: Most bromides are soluble in water
rules.note: Silver bromide is a pale yellow precipitate used in photographic film

rules.rule: Most iodides are soluble in water
rules.note: Silver iodide is yellow and insoluble even in ammonia

rules.rule: Most fluorides are soluble, but the alkaline earth and lead fluorides are not
rules.note: Barium fluoride is sparingly soluble and is used in toothpaste

rules.rule: Most hydroxides are insoluble
rules.exceptions: exceptions: group 1 and NH₄⁺, slightly soluble Sr²⁺ and Ba²⁺
rules.note: Group 1 hydroxides are strong bases, so they dissolve freely

rules.rule: Most sulfides are insoluble
rules.exceptions: exceptions: group 1, NH₄⁺ and several heavy transition metals
rules.note: Sulfides of the group 1 metals react with water to give hydrogen sulfide

rules.rule: Most carbonates are insoluble
rules.note: Carbonate reacts with acid to give the fizzing carbon dioxide test

rules.rule: Bicarbonates dissolve only as their dissolved solid, so the ion is stable in solution but unstable as a salt
rules.note: Heating bicarbonate gives the carbonate, water and carbon dioxide

rules.rule: Most phosphates are insoluble
rules.note: Phosphate is the main nutrient in bone and tooth enamel

rules.rule: Hydrogen phosphate salts are mostly insoluble
rules.note: This is the dominant phosphate species at neutral pH

rules.rule: Dihydrogen phosphate salts are soluble in water
rules.note: The acid form of phosphate, used in food and buffers

rules.rule: Arsenates mostly follow the phosphate rules
rules.note: Silver arsenate is a chocolate brown precipitate used in the Marsh test

rules.rule: Most oxalates are insoluble or slightly soluble
rules.exceptions: exceptions: group 1, NH₄⁺; Ca²⁺ is slightly soluble
rules.note: Calcium oxalate is the insoluble core of many kidney stones

rules.rule: Most chromates are insoluble
rules.note: Silver chromate is brick red and changes to dichromate in acid

rules.rule: Dichromates are mostly soluble
rules.note: Chromate and dichromate interconvert in acid and alkali

rules.rule: Most iodates are insoluble
rules.note: Silver iodate is a white precipitate

rules.rule: Potassium and sodium permanganate are soluble
rules.note: The ion is deeply purple and self indicating in titrations

rules.rule: Borates of the group 1 metals and ammonium are soluble
rules.note: Boric acid is a weak acid that acts as a Lewis acid

rules.rule: Most silicates are insoluble
rules.note: Water glass is sodium silicate solution, and silica is a very weak acid

rules.rule: Thiosulfates of the group 1 metals and ammonium are soluble
rules.note: Decomposes slowly to give a yellow sulphur precipitate

rules.rule: Most phenoxides are soluble in water
rules.note: Phenoxide is a much weaker base than hydroxide
